key_insight: Long-range circuit noise fragility depends on fault-phase interference with the target Hamiltonian, not simply on how far faults spread.
engineering_relevance: Ansatz design should balance expressivity and gate-count exposure while controlling transverse operations that activate otherwise energetically dark faults.
method: Prove contrasting energy damage from equally extensive faults in Heisenberg chains.
Test catalyst suppression and annealing in noisy training with full-width long-range ZZ gates.
Predict noise-induced energy shifts using single-fault fragility and gate-count exposure λ = pK.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an exact N/2 damage ratio for equal-support faults, halved dephasing error when both catalysts are suppressed, and rescue of every tested trapped trajectory through catalyst annealing.
watch_item: Generality beyond the studied Heisenberg-chain circuits and noise settings requires validation.
paper_title: Phase Interference and Transverse Catalysts Govern the Noise Fragility of Long-Range Variational Quantum Circuits
